title: SLI granularity and cost tradeoffs for bursty inference
body:
Purpose and scope

Quick primer: this note collects our thinking about the right SLI aggregation granularity for LLM inference paths that experience highly bursty traffic (microbursts from fan-out, sudden tenant spikes). It ties SLI windows to query budget/cost targets and recommends a sampling + probe strategy that keeps dashboard query cost manageable.

Audience: observability, SRE, runtime-product, and any team owning model rollouts.

High-level problem statement
- Bursty inference makes per-minute SLIs noisy; 1m SLOs either blow up or are dominated by tail noise.
- Coarse aggregation (1h) hides short lived regressions and makes rollbacks slow.
- Fine aggregation (1s-10s) is prohibitively expensive to compute at full fidelity across tenants.
- We need a hybrid approach that surfaces real regressions quickly while bounding query cost.

Design principles (ranked)
1) Detect actionable regressions within 5–15 minutes for production rollouts.
2) Keep query cost for the observability stack under the budget (see cost section).
3) Maintain tenant isolation for top customers (dedicated SLIs per committed tiers).
4) Make sampling deterministic and reproducible for incident investigation.

Suggested SLI tiers and aggregation windows
- Fast detection SLI (probe-driven): 1m rolling window, evaluated on synthetic + stratified probes (see probe plan). Only stored for 7 days, used by oncall and rollout gating.
- Operational SLI (cohort-backed): 5–15m rolling windows, computed for tenant cohorts (top-20 tenants, dev/stage, all-other). Retain 30d.
- Business SLI (aggregate): 1h/24h windows for billing/exec dashboards, 90d retention.

Concrete SLI definitions (examples)
- TTFToken_95: 95th percentile time-to-first-token per request path (chat vs single-turn) — compute over 1m probe window and over 15m operational window.
- GenLatency_p99_by_tenant: 99th percentile per-tenant generation latency sampled per 5m (only for top-20 tenants)
- ColdCache_failure_rate: fraction of requests requiring cold-model-load or KV-prefetch that exceed 1s extra latency; 15m window
- ModelFallback_rate: rate of requests that hit fallback (cheaper model) due to capacity, 5m window
- TokenCost_per_request: average token compute cost per request (micro-billing unit), 1h window for finance, 15m for ops when investigating regressions

Why these windows?
- The 1m probe window lets us surface regressions triggered by a deployment or external event quickly. But storing 1m for all tenants is too expensive; we do probes + top-tenant sampling.
- 5–15m windows smooth short microbursts yet remain actionable for rollouts. 15m is the default operational window.

Sampling and probe strategy
- Deterministic stratified sampling: hash(request.customer_id) mod 1000 to pick a 1/100 sample for long-term metrics. This keeps reproducibility for repro.
- Top-tenant full fidelity: top-20 revenue/criticality tenants get full retention and per-request indexing for 30 days.
- Synthetic probes: emulate 3 traffic classes (short prompt, long prompt, multi-hop) and run every 30s from multiple regions. Probes are tagged and pinned to canary deployments to test rollout behavior.
- Adaptive probe amplification: if probes detect a 2x increase in p95 latency vs baseline, double probe cadence for 20 minutes to capture the regression.

Trace anchoring and span design notes
- Anchor span id = request_id for each external call; include fields: model_variant, kernel_variant, kv_cache_hit, tenant_tier, route (hosted/dedicated/private). Keep these in root span tags.
- Key spans to emit: request-scheduler (enqueue/dequeue), model-loader (cold/warm), runtime-exec (start_token/end_token), kv-cache-lookup.
- Emit sampling decision and probe-tag in span: sampling.policy and probe.type. Enables trace filtering for probes vs live requests.
- Trace retention: keep full traces for top tenants and probes for 30d; for remaining tenants keep sampled traces (~1/1000) for 7d.

Dashboard composition guidelines
- Dashboards should be tier-aware (global overview -> cohort -> tenant drilldown). Avoid a single global p99 panel for all tenants.
- Recommended panels for rollout dashboard:
  - Probe timeline (p50/p95/p99) with baseline overlay
  - Top-20 tenants p95 comparison sparkline (5m)
  - Model fallback and capacity throttle rate (5m)
  - KV-cache warmth heatmap (tenant vs time)
  - Cost per token trend with 24h smoothing
- Query cost optimizations: pre-aggregate per-minute rollups into a metrics store for 15m/1h windows. Avoid ad-hoc raw-event scans for oncall panels.

Alerting heuristics (practical)
- Fast-signal alert (pager): Probe p95 exceeds baseline by 2.5x AND probe-error-rate > 0.5% for 3 consecutive rounds (3m).
- Tenant-specific alert (ticketing only): Top-tenant p99 > SLA threshold for 25m. Pager escalation only if more than 3 top tenants are affected.
- Cost-surge alert: TokenCost_per_request increases > 30% vs 24h median and sustained for 1h. Pager to infra/cost-ops on unusual spend.

Cost budget and query-count targets (back of envelope)
- Goal: keep observability queries < 10% of infra costs. Rough numbers:
  - Storing 1m probes for 3 classes + top-20 full telemetry = estimated 12k metrics series/day.
  - Query cadence for oncall dashboards + synthetic probes: ~1200 queries/day.
  - If query costs exceed target, escalate to reduce retention or widen aggregation windows.

Runbook snippets (quick step list)
- If probe p95 spikes: 1) Confirm if spike is probe-only (filter probe.type), 2) Check recent deploys and canary tagging, 3) Check model-loader spans for cold loads, 4) Run kv-cache warmth report for affected tenants, 5) If widespread, trigger rollback or scale dedicated pools.
- If top-tenant p99 high but global fine: 1) pull tenant trace, 2) compare tenant's recent prompt-length distribution, 3) check throttling/rate-limit traces, 4) open SEV ticket with tenant success.

Open questions and TODOs
- Need an implementation cost estimate for pre-aggregated minute rollups in our metrics store. Arjun to run numbers against PromScale and BigQuery.
- Decide retention differential for private deployments (customers may request longer trace retention). Need legal/infra input.
- NVMe-backed KV-cache instrumentation: what metric for "warmth" maps best to ops investigation? eviction_count vs prefix_hit_ratio? Lina to prototype.
- How to quickly correlate token-cost anomalies to model-quantization changes across rollout graph? Consider emitting model-shape + quantization tags at request time.

Notes-to-self / messy brainstorming (keep)
- Could we use ephemeral sampling boost for tenants that just failed probes? Eg give them temporary higher sampling to catch a regression. Would increase cost but aids triage.
- Thinking: use retval of runtime-exec span to compute per-token CPU surrogate when GPU metrics not available. Experiment idea.

Appendix: example metrics queries (psuedo-SQL)
- Probe p95 (1m):
  SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) AS p95
  FROM metrics.probe_requests
  WHERE probe.type = 'multi-hop' AND region = 'us-west1'
  GROUP BY tumbling_window(1 minute)

- Top-tenant p95 (5m):
  SELECT tenant_id, percentile(gen_latency_ms, 95) AS p95
  FROM events.requests_sampled
  WHERE tenant_id IN (SELECT top_tenants FROM config.top_20)
  GROUP BY tenant_id, tumbling_window(5 minute)

End
